title: WPSS/539/2014 of Nidhi Bhandari Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
1. Writ Petition (S/S) No. 539 of 2014
Nidhi Bhandari Ö Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
With
2. Writ Petition (S/S) No. 540 of 2014
Deep Chand ÖPetitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
Present: Mr. Rakesh Thapaliyal, Advocate with Mr. Niranjan
Bhatt, Advocate, present for the petitioners.
Mr. N.P. Shah, learned Standing Counsel, present for
the State/respondent nos.1 to 3 & 5, 6 & 7.
 Mr. Amar Shukla, Advocate, present for the respondent
no. 4.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. Since the issue involved in these writ petitions is
same, both the writ petitions are disposed of with a
common order.
2. The petitioners in both the above writ petitions
are Primary School Teachers, who were appointed as such
vide order dated 8th February, 2014 and 7th February,
2014, respectively. Subsequently, their services have been
terminated vide order dated 01.04.2014 and 02.04.2014
respectively passed by the appointing authority. Aggrieved,
the petitioners have filed present writ petition before this
Court.

2
3. Counter and rejoinder affidavits have been
exchanged in the matter, hence the matter is being heard
finally.
4. The brief background of the case which would be
necessary at this juncture is as under:-
5. After the Right to Education becoming a
fundamental right and was inserted in Part III of the
Constitution of India as Article 21A and later the
Parliament having enacted the law known as ìthe Right of
Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009î,
not only the entire elementary education (Class I to VIII)
has now become compulsory and a fundamental right of a
child, but it has also to become a ìmeaningfulî education
as well.
6. Under the provisions of the Right to Education
Act, a Government of India body, known as ìNational
Council for Teachers Educationî (from hereinafter referred
to as the ìNCTEî) has been given the responsibility to frame
the guidelines, qualifications etc. for teachers who have to
teach such elementary classes.
7. Consequent to the above, the National Council
for Teachers Education had published a notification on 23rd
August, 2010 whereby qualifications were laid down for
teachers in primary schools i.e. elementary school as well
as senior elementary schools. Inter alia, the qualifications
are that a candidate must be trained in elementary
education. In Uttarakhand State, this training or certificate
is given after two years of successful completion of
elementary teachers training and it is known as ìBasic
Teaching Certificateî (from herein after referred to as
ìBTCî).

3
8. Apart from a candidate being a graduate and
BTC trained, he further has to successfully qualify an
examination which is known as ìTeachers Eligibility Testî
(from herein after referred to as the ìTETî). TET is
conducted by the State Government as well as by Central
Board of Secondary Education which is known as ìCentral
Teachers Eligibility Testî (from herein after referred to as
the ìCTETî). For a general candidate the minimum
qualifying marks in the test is 60% whereas it is 50% in
case of Schedule Caste and Schedule Tribes and OBC
candidates. And here lies the catch!
9. Both the petitioners before this Court claim that
they belong to a community which is known as ìRawaltaî,
and a notification to this effect was issued by the
Government of Uttarakhand on 31st January, 2004
whereby all the persons belonging to ìRawalta/Jaunpuriî
Community in District Uttarkashi were declared as ìOBCî.
10. The petitioners, however, were not having an
OBC Certificate but they appeared in the TET examination
which is known as ìCTETî and in the said examination
they scored 157 out of 300 and 81 out of 150 respectively.
Since the petitioners were not having an OBC certificate,
they were treated as a General category candidate. They
were only subsequently given an OBC Certificate on
01.01.2014.
11. The Government of Uttarakhand vide notification
dated 18.01.2014, published certain posts of Primary
School Teacher for District Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand in
which the petitioners applied as an OBC candidate and
they were selected and subsequently appointed as such.
Thereafter, the impugned orders dated 01.04.2014 and

4
02.04.2014 were passed whereby it was said that the OBC
Certificate which were only issued on the basis of
Government Order dated 19.11.2013 whereas the
petitioners had done their Teachers Eligibility Test prior to
that date as General category candidate and since they
have not secured 60% marks but only 50% marks, they
cannot be held to have qualified TET. The fact, however, is
that in each of the cases the petitioners have secured
appointment as Primary School teacher as an OBC
candidate.
12. The learned counsel for the petitioners relied
upon an order of a learned Single Judge of this Court dated
14.07.2014, passed in Writ Petition No.1614 (SS) of 2014,
wherein the learned Single Judge has held that the
ìRawalta/Jaunpuri Communityî was declared as an OBC
Community way back in the year 2004 by a Government
Order dated 31.01.2004 and Government Order dated
19.11.2013 on the basis of which termination orders have
been passed against the petitioners, is only an explanatory
order. The actual rights were given by the Government
Order dated 31.01.2004 and, therefore, it is wrong to say
that only a prospective benefit of Government Order dated
19.11.2013 will be given to the petitioners. The fact that
the petitioners belong to ìRawalta Communityî is not in
doubt. They were declared as members of OBC community
vide Government Order dated 31.01.2004. Consequently,
the petitioners were declared member of OBC community.
A Certificate is only a proof of the fact which existed even
prior to the issuance of this Certificate.
13. Therefore, holding that rights only accrued in
favour of the petitioners vide Government Order dated 19th
November, 2013 is wrong. The clear notification to this

5
effect was issued as far back as on 31.01.2004, the
impugned orders do not disclose the correct legal position
in the matter.
14. Moreover the impugned orders dispensing with
the service of the petitioners have been passed without
giving any opportunity of hearing to the petitioners and
also in view of the fact that Government Order dated 19th
November, 2013 has been held to be only explanatory by
the learned Single Judge of this Court and the actual rights
have been given from the Government Order dated 31st
January, 2004.
15. In view of the above mentioned facts and
circumstances, these two writ petitions are allowed. The
impugned orders dated 01.04.2014 and 02.04.2014,
terminating the services of the petitioners are quashed.
State Authorities/Respondents shall immediately give
appointment to the petitioners as Primary School Teacher
and shall give entire backwages from the due date.
16. No order as to costs.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 16.07.2014
ML
